newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Murtaza supporters want Bhutto barred from polls.
newsitem.headline: Murtaza supporters want Bhutto barred from polls.

text.p: Supporters of Murtaza Bhutto, slain brother of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, on Tuesday demanded that she and her ministers be banned from standing in a general election set for February.

"They (the Bhutto government) looted and plundered the wealth of the country...They should be punished and disqualified from taking part in the next election," Rao Rasheed, secretary general of Murtaza's breakaway faction of the Pakistan People's Party, told reporters.
Murtaza, the estranged younger brother of Benazir Bhutto, was killed by police in Karachi on September 20.

Police said they fired after his bodyguards began shooting. Murtaza supporters blamed the government. Bhutto herself said the killing was a part of a conspiracy against her family and government, but did not name the plotters.
Rasheed said politicians and bureaucrats should be held accountable for alleged corruption.
President Farooq Leghari dismissed the Bhutto government in the early hours of Tuesday on charges of corruption and misrule.
Rasheed said his party welcomed Leghari's decision, which he said had fullfilled a demand of Murtaza Bhutto.

"The Benazir-Zardari government wanted to cover up the murder of chairman Murtaza Bhutto and his comrades and used the incident to defame the president and the army. Now we look for justice and punishment for those involved in the killings."
Rasheed said Leghari should also dismiss the four provincial governments and appoint neutral governors and chief ministers.
"We demand the release of all our workers and other political prisioners of other political parties," he added.
